title: Return only the sections a pickup needs
lead: `slicer next --show --json` and `slicer next --ready --json` both send every section body. The text form of `--ready` is already short, and the skill tells agents to use `--json`, so they pay for the full slice on every pickup.
**Not in this slice:** the agent skill text, `next --show`, the TUI, or dropping `--ready`'s full slice when no section is named.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: An agent that follows the published loop receives the whole item and every section. `next --ready` was added to bound that pickup, but its JSON still assigns `slice` to the full slice record, including lead, notes, and every section body. Asking for `show --section` afterwards is a second turn. The call that saves credits is one command: identity, dependencies, effective score, path, the scope boundary, and only the section bodies the work needs. `--json --lean` already drops empty scaffolding and has to apply to that payload.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/cli.py` (`next --ready`, and the shared `--section` / `--lean` emit path)
- `tests/test_ready.py`
- `docs/agents.md`, `README.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md` for the new flag

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `slicer next --ready --section "Implement" --section "Check" --json` returns item identity, dependencies, effective score, path, the scope boundary, and those two section bodies. Other section bodies, the lead, and notes are absent.
2. `slicer next --ready --json` with no `--section` still returns the full slice record it returns today.
3. An unknown heading exits the same way `slicer show --section` does for an unknown heading. `--section` on `next` without `--ready`, and `--ready` together with `--show`, stay usage errors. An empty queue is unchanged (`item: null`, exit 2).
4. `--json --lean` on the limited payload drops empty `depends_on`, an empty `blocked` list, and a null path, and it keeps the requested section bodies.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Add a repeatable `--section` on `next` that is valid only with `--ready`. Use the same heading match as `show --section`. When one or more headings are given and the item has a slice, the JSON slice carries the scope boundary and those sections only. When `--section` is omitted, keep today's full slice so current `--ready` callers do not change. A row with no slice still reports that it needs `promote` and does not invent sections. Run the payload through the existing lean emitter when `--json --lean` is set. Leave the text form of `--ready` as identity, boundary, and headings. Update the command reference so the flag is discoverable.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The four cases above pass. `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` and `slicer check` pass. A pickup with `--section` is smaller than `next --show --json` for the same slice because the other section bodies are not in the output.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit. Do not tag or push.
